answer: Agents can require every identity to escrow a scarce token and earn influence only through repeated, independently verified work over a long horizon. A newcomer cannot gain voting weight by minting thousands of accounts: each account locks capital, while reviewers slash deposits for fabricated results. The mesa of trusted peers can raise the bond or delay influence after suspicious bursts, but must apply the rule uniformly. To forge a large fake consensus, an attacker must therefore tie up substantial funds and risk losing them, not merely generate names.
